test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 7 Oct 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
A football player got fractured while playing football. He went to the hospital. The doctor took 'X' substance and mixed it with water for supporting the fractured bones in the right position. 

What is the name of substance 'X'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Plaster of Paris**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plaster of Paris is a quick-setting gypsum plaster consisting of a fine white powder (calcium sulfate hemihydrate).
 
• When mixed with water, it forms a paste that hardens quickly, providing support to fractured bones.
 
• It is widely used in medical applications for making casts to immobilize broken bones while they heal.
 
• The compound is formed by heating gypsum (calcium sulfate dihydrate) to about 150°C (300°F).
 
• Plaster of Paris is also used in arts and crafts, as well as for architectural moldings and other decorative elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gypsum**

 
 
• Gypsum is a naturally occurring mineral composed of calcium sulfate dihydrate.
 
• It is used in various industries, including construction (for drywall and plaster), agriculture (as a soil conditioner), and food (as a coagulant in tofu).
 
• Gypsum can be transformed into Plaster of Paris by heating it to remove water content.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Sulfate**
 
 
• Calcium sulfate is a chemical compound with the formula CaSO₄.
 
• It appears in nature as the mineral gypsum and can be converted to Plaster of Paris by heating.
 
• Calcium sulfate is used in the production of cement, plaster, and as a food additive.
 
 
 
• **Orthopedic Casts**
 
 
• Orthopedic casts are medical devices used to immobilize and protect a broken bone while it heals.
 
• Casts are typically made from Plaster of Paris or fiberglass materials.
 
• They provide a rigid and stable environment to ensure proper bone alignment during the healing process.
 
 
 
• **Setting Reaction**
 
 
• When Plaster of Paris is mixed with water, it undergoes an exothermic reaction, rehydrating to form gypsum.
 
• This reaction causes the mixture to harden quickly, making it ideal for medical and construction applications.
 
• The setting time can be controlled by adding various additives to the mixture.
